synopsis: LiDAR-EVS is a March 2026 neural reconstruction preprint that renders lidar as well as cameras, with cited evidence limited to on-road settings [f3817, f4009]. It claims lidar Chamfer distances 48.6% and 47.2% lower than SplatAD at a 3 m lateral shift, but absolute values were not extracted [f4009]. Across the job-site, sensor-simulation and glossary discussions, moving or extrapolated sensor viewpoints remain a challenge; LiDAR-EVS attributes extrapolation failure to single-traversal training and severe overfitting [f4010, f4023, f4518, f16004]. LiDAR-EVS and VEGS attempt to remedy novel-path reconstruction problems, but the corpus does not establish that those problems have disappeared [f4012]. Reported minimal real-to-sim gaps in NeuroNCAP are therefore in tension with critics’ concerns about weak extrapolation and lack of harsh-weather support in LiHi-GS and LiDAR-EVS; the supplied evidence does not establish off-road applicability [f5076, f3817, f4518].

relations.note: Both identify poor generalisation to novel or extrapolated viewpoints.
